Rank order is EVIDENCE-LED: the shared-management edge is first because all three located anchors treat hydrocele and spermatocele as one entity, while the reproductive edge is SECOND because its principal content is an ABSENCE of association.

IDENTITY-REFUSAL, DECLARED: NO EDGE TO epididymal-cyst HAS BEEN REGISTERED, deliberately. A spermatocele is an epididymal cyst containing sperm, so the relationship between these two catalog identities is TAXONOMIC CONTAINMENT rather than a secondary condition, and an edge would misrepresent a category relationship as a clinical association. The two identities remain distinct, neither is an alias of the other, and the located ultrasound and pathology literature distinguishes them, with one located anchor reporting pathologists identifying 29 spermatoceles and 22 epididymal cysts in the same series.

DIRECTION GUARD, APPLIED TO BOTH EDGES: neither edge asserts that a spermatocele causes anything. The varicocele-hydrocele edge registers CO-OCCURRENCE AND SHARED SURGICAL MANAGEMENT, and the hypogonadism edge registers a NULL together with a transient post-procedure effect. Both are written so they cannot be cited as evidence that a spermatocele causes disease.

SCOPE GUARD, APPLIED TO THE NULL EDGE: the located null is a null for SMALL lesions, with a median size of 4 mm, and the comparison is age-confounded because men with lesions were significantly older. It must not be read as a null for large symptomatic spermatoceles, and the same series reports significant improvement in sperm count and neutral alpha-glucosidase after surgery in lesions larger than 2.5 cm.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Hydrocele and spermatocele are managed as a SINGLE SCROTAL FLUID-COLLECTION PATHWAY in the located urological surgical literature, and every located anchor treats them together rather than separately. A prospective comparative analysis of outpatient against inpatient hydrocele and spermatocele surgery opened by defining both as FLUID COLLECTIONS WITHIN THE SCROTUM and noted that because a lack of therapeutic guidelines, treatment is largely based on clinical experience, with surgery the gold standard in German-speaking countries; in 82 prospectively assigned patients, the OUTPATIENT COHORT SHOWED A SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER RATE OF CLAVIEN-DINDO III DEGREE COMPLICATIONS (p LESS THAN 0.05) and required antibiotic therapy, a Clavien-Dindo II degree event, significantly more often (p EQUALS 0.002), leading the authors to conclude that outpatient surgery should be questioned (PMID 42295361). A Scandinavian audit of complications after scrotal surgery, in which GOLD STANDARD TREATMENT OF SYMPTOMATIC HYDROCELE OR SPERMATOCELE IS SURGERY, found in a first 12-month period that 22 of 65 operated men contacted the department postoperatively for swelling or pain, 19 were examined and SIX WERE RE-OPERATED ONE TO NINE TIMES, and in the following year 16 of 69 contacted the department, 13 were examined and five re-operated, with significantly fewer complications when patients were examined preoperatively and informed by a SPECIALISED UROLOGIST rather than by residents and interns (p EQUALS 0.012) (PMID 33569989). A German management review states that treatment indications for hydrocele and spermatocele are based on diagnosis with high-resolution ultrasonography, that ASYMPTOMATIC FINDINGS DO NOT NEED CORRECTION, and that in younger men the wish for children must be taken into account as both procedures may lead to infertility, especially spermatocele resection, which may lead to EPIDIDYMAL OBSTRUCTION (PMID 24806800). Recorded as documented association only, with the fact that no located anchor reports a paired co-occurrence rate, carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and THE ASSOCIATION IS CO-OCCURRENCE, NOT CONSEQUENCE: hydrocele and spermatocele are both fluid collections in the scrotum, and the located evidence reports them as a combined surgical category rather than as two diseases with a causal link. NO LOCATED ANCHOR REPORTS HOW OFTEN A SPERMATOCELE COEXISTS WITH A HYDROCELE, and none reports a prevalence for either, so this edge carries a shared-management finding and a shared-complication finding and no magnitude. The first anchor's 82 patients were prospectively assigned to outpatient and inpatient groups and pooled hydrocele with spermatocele, so its complication rates are combined-procedure rates that cannot be attributed to either procedure separately, and the authors frame treatment as based on clinical experience because a lack of therapeutic guidelines. The second anchor is an AUDIT OF COMPLICATIONS with two consecutive cohorts and a re-operation rate of six in 65 and five in 69, where the re-operations were driven by bleeding and infection under the authors' stated focus on perioperative haemostasis and postoperative activity restriction, and where a lower re-operation rate for the specialist-urologist group is a service finding rather than a biological one. The third anchor is a NARRATIVE MANAGEMENT REVIEW that establishes the treatment-indication principle and the fertility caution, and it is the only anchor that names epididymal obstruction as a specific risk. Individual claims require a dated high-resolution scrotal ultrasonography documenting each collection separately, a documented operative report identifying which procedure was performed, a dated fertility assessment with a pre-operative semen analysis where reproductive plans are relevant, and a clinical determination separating a spermatocele from a hydrocele, from an epididymal cyst and from a varicocele, all of which are differentiated by ultrasound criteria the located anchors do not set out.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is shared mechanical and hydrostatic loading in a confined scrotal compartment: both conditions are fluid accumulations within a closed anatomical space, and an accumulation in one region raises pressure and displaces the surrounding structures, so a second collection in the same compartment is mechanically plausible and the two are consequently approached by the same operative route through the same scrotal approach and the same tunica or epididymal dissection, which is why the located literature manages them as one entity; the vector is named as shared compartmental loading and a shared operative route rather than as a lymphatic, secretory or obstructive mechanism, because the located anchors are surgical and describe management rather than pathogenesis and none offers an aetiological account.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at prospective-comparative-surgical-cohort, retrospective-complications-audit and narrative-management-review class, following the file's existing urologic and treatment-related pathway scope. All three anchors treat hydrocele and spermatocele as one combined entity, and the first states outright that both are fluid collections within the scrotum, which is the located basis for registering them as a shared pathway rather than as a causal relationship (PMID 42295361). The audit is registered because it is the located source with the most concrete complication data, six re-operations among 65 men with one to nine re-operations each in the first period, and it is also the source of the service finding that fewer complications followed preoperative assessment by a specialist urologist (PMID 33569989). The management review is registered because it supplies the two operative principles this edge depends on, that asymptomatic findings need no correction, and that in younger men fertility wishes must be weighed because spermatocele resection may cause epididymal obstruction (PMID 24806800). Because all three are surgical and management sources, none reports co-occurrence, and the conservative standard holds the edge at association only with no magnitude.

THE ASSOCIATION IS CO-OCCURRENCE RATHER THAN CONSEQUENCE: both are fluid collections in the scrotum and the located evidence reports them as a combined surgical category, not as a causal relationship, and the mechanism claim is correspondingly limited to shared compartmental loading and a shared operative route. THE FIRST ANCHOR POOLS THE TWO PROCEDURES, so its 82 patients and its Clavien-Dindo III and II rates are COMBINED-PROCEDURE RATES that cannot be attributed to either procedure separately, and the authors state that treatment is largely based on clinical experience because a LACK OF THERAPEUTIC GUIDELINES (PMID 42295361). THE SECOND ANCHOR IS AN AUDIT DRIVEN BY A COMPLICATION CLUSTER, in which re-operations followed bleeding and infection under the authors' stated focus on perioperative haemostasis and postoperative activity restriction, and its finding of fewer complications after specialist preoperative assessment (p EQUALS 0.012) is a SERVICE finding rather than a biological one (PMID 33569989). THE THIRD ANCHOR IS A NARRATIVE MANAGEMENT REVIEW available only in German in the source database and contributes treatment-indication and fertility principles rather than data (PMID 24806800). NO located anchor sets out the ultrasonographic criteria that separate a spermatocele from a hydrocele, from an epididymal cyst and from a varicocele, so an individual claim cannot rest on the located literature for its imaging diagnosis, and no anchor reports a re-operation rate attributable to epididymal obstruction specifically.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: An epididymal cyst, which is a distinct catalog identity and which the located ultrasound literature treats as a separate entity from a spermatocele even though the two share an origin, so misclassification between them is a live alternative to co-occurrence with a hydrocele

Varicocele, which is a dilated pampiniform plexus rather than a fluid collection and which is reported in the located ultrasound literature as a separate scrotal finding, sometimes subclinical, and which the located anchors do not separate from hydrocele in their pooled reporting
Haematocele, which is a post-traumatic or post-surgical blood collection in the scrotal wall and which is the differential for an acute postoperative scrotal swelling of the kind the audit reports
Infection, which the audit identifies as one of the two drivers of re-operation and which can produce or enlarge a collection independently of any pre-existing spermatocele
Prior scrotal surgery, which is a reported cause of postoperative hydrocele and which would produce a hydrocele temporally unrelated to any spermatocele

sourceReferences.note: PROSPECTIVE COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS of 82 patients prospectively assigned to outpatient and inpatient HYDROCele AND SPERMATOCELE SURGERY, with postoperative complications recorded by Clavien-Dindo classification at 30 days. DISCLOSED: this article is in German with a German abstract, the two procedures are POOLED so the complication rates are combined-procedure rates, and the condition is therefore a shared pathway rather than a causal relationship.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: This edge is registered for its NULL and that null is its principal content: across the located evidence, a spermatocele is NOT associated with impaired reproductive function. In a cohort of 861 men presenting for fertility evaluation with a semen analysis and scrotal ultrasonography between 2002 and 2022, in whom EPIDIDYMAL CYST LESIONS INCLUDE BOTH SPERMATOCELES AND EPIDIDYMAL CYSTS, 164 men (19 percent) had a unilateral right lesion with a median size of 4 mm, 189 (22 percent) a unilateral left lesion with a median of 4 mm, and 113 (13 percent) bilateral lesions; men WITH LESIONS WERE SIGNIFICANTLY OLDER THAN MEN WITHOUT but showed NO STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCE in semen volume, sperm concentration, sperm motility, sperm morphology, total motile sperm count, OR SERUM HORMONAL VALUES including testosterone and follicle-stimulating hormone, and lesion SIZE AND LATERALITY DID NOT SIGNIFICANTLY CORRELATE with any semen parameter evaluated (PMID 39186830). In a prospective evaluation of microsurgical epididymal cystectomy in 51 men with fertility requirements, in whom PATHOLOGISTS IDENTIFIED 29 SPERMATOCELES AND 22 EPIDIDYMAL CYSTS, there was an INSIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCE in sperm count, motility, morphology or neutral alpha-glucosidase between pre-operation and post-operation at 1 year, with the complication rate 7.3 percent and no recurrence during follow-up (PMID 30142407). In a series of 69 patients undergoing 114 alcohol sclerotherapy procedures for hydrocele and spermatocele with an overall success rate of 97.62 percent, POST-SCLEROTHERAPY SPERMOGRAMS REVEALED REDUCTION of concentration, motility and morphology UP TO 6 MONTHS, with return to normal parameters by the 12th month after the procedure (PMID 21756377). Recorded as documented association only, with the null and the transient treatment effect both carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and THE LOCATED EVIDENCE POINTS THE OTHER WAY, so this edge exists to record an ABSENCE of association rather than a presence. The primary anchor is an explicit null study: it is titled as finding no association, its conclusion is that patients should be counselled toward conservative management with observation for asymptomatic lesions, and it reports no difference in ANY semen parameter and no difference in SERUM HORMONAL VALUES. Two qualifications prevent that null from being over-read, and both are recorded: men with lesions were significantly older, which is an age-confounded comparison in a cohort where age itself depresses semen parameters, and the median lesion size was 4 mm, so the null is a null for SMALL lesions and does not extend to large symptomatic spermatoceles. The second anchor is a postoperative study in which the primary claim is surgical efficacy and the reproductive finding is a secondary non-inferiority observation, and it also contains a partial counterfinding, sperm count and neutral alpha-glucosidase were significantly INCREASED after surgery in patients with lesions larger than 2.5 cm. The third anchor reports a TRANSIENT treatment effect, with sperm parameters reduced for up to 6 months after sclerotherapy and normalised by 12 months, so an individual evaluated early after sclerotherapy would show a different picture from one evaluated later, and the located evidence does not establish that the reduction is fully reversible in every patient. Individual claims require a dated high-resolution scrotal ultrasonography with lesion size and laterality documented, a dated semen analysis with the abstinence interval recorded, serum testosterone and follicle-stimulating hormone measured, a documented surgical or sclerotherapy history with the dates, and a clinical determination separating an incidental small lesion from a large symptomatic one and separating any post-procedure effect from a pre-existing one.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is the mechanical one that the located evidence tested and did not support: a spermatocele is a sperm-containing retention cyst of the epididymal duct, and the concern has been that such a cyst compresses or obstructs the epididymal outflow, raises scrotal temperature, or diverts sperm, any of which would depress count, motility or morphology. The located evidence examined precisely that vector in 861 men with ultrasound-confirmed lesions, stratified by size and laterality, and found no signal in any semen parameter or in serum testosterone or follicle-stimulating hormone; the vector is therefore named as a proposed mechanism that was tested and not demonstrated, which is why the mechanism category is NOT_ESTABLISHED rather than a positive category, and the only positive reproductive signal in the located evidence is a transient post-procedure change that reversed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at retrospective-cohort-with-null-finding, prospective-postoperative-cohort and uncontrolled-treatment-series class, following the file's existing urologic, hormonal and treatment-related pathway scope. The null cohort is the anchor that carries the whole edge: 861 men with 466 lesions, no difference in any semen parameter or in serum hormonal values, and no correlation with lesion size or laterality, with its own conclusion counselling conservative management and observation for asymptomatic lesions (PMID 39186830). Its two qualifications, the significant age difference between men with and without lesions and the 4 mm median lesion size, are stated on the face of the edge so the null cannot be read as a null for large symptomatic lesions. The postoperative cohort is registered because it independently reports no significant change in sperm count, motility, morphology or neutral alpha-glucosidase at 1 year in a series in which pathologists distinguished 29 spermatoceles from 22 epididymal cysts, which is the located confirmation that the null is not an artefact of mixing the two lesion types (PMID 30142407). The sclerotherapy series is registered for the transient treatment effect, a reduction in concentration, motility and morphology up to 6 months with normalisation by 12 months, which is the reason the edge records a time course rather than a flat null (PMID 21756377). Because the anchor evidence is predominantly null and the only positive signal is a reversible treatment effect, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only with an explicitly negative result.

THE NULL IS AGE-CONFOUNDED IN ITS COMPARISON: men WITH lesions were significantly OLDER than men without at the time of evaluation, and age itself depresses semen parameters, so the comparison is not age-adjusted within the analysis as described (PMID 39186830). THE NULL IS A NULL FOR SMALL LESIONS: the median lesion size was 4 MM with interquartile ranges of 3 to 8 and 3 to 9 mm, so the finding does not extend to large symptomatic spermatoceles, and the second anchor's significant improvements in sperm count and neutral alpha-glucosidase in lesions LARGER THAN 2.5 CM are a partial counterfinding to it (PMID 39186830, PMID 30142407). THE SECOND ANCHOR'S PRIMARY CLAIM IS SURGICAL EFFICACY, with the reproductive finding a secondary non-inferiority observation, and it reports 29 SPERMATOCELES AND 22 EPIDIDYMAL CYSTS distinguished by pathologists, so the two lesion types are separable in that series (PMID 30142407). NO located anchor reports a hypogonadism DIAGNOSIS rate, a testosterone threshold, a follicle-stimulating hormone threshold, or any hormonal axis other than testosterone and follicle-stimulating hormone, and no located anchor reports outcomes in men presenting with a large, painful or long-standing spermatocele.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Age-related decline in semen parameters, which the primary anchor's own comparison shows operated on: men with lesions were significantly older, and age independently depresses count, motility and morphology

A pre-existing or concurrent cause of impaired fertility, including a partner factor, a prior vasectomy or its reversal, an undescended testis, or a systemic endocrine or genetic condition, none of which the located anchors adjust for

The transient effect of sclerotherapy or of surgery itself, which the located series reports as a reduction in concentration, motility and morphology for up to 6 months, so timing of the assessment relative to the procedure is decisive

An intratesticular or paratesticular neoplasm masquerading as or complicating a scrotal cyst, which the located anchors do not address and which must be excluded by ultrasonography and, where indicated, histopathology before any of these findings is attributed to a spermatocele

A coexisting varicocele, which the primary anchor explicitly recorded as present or subclinical on its ultrasound protocol and which independently depresses semen parameters and was not analysed as a separate variable

PALPATED CYST PAIN WAS PRESENT IN 32 OF 51, and PATHOLOGISTS IDENTIFIED 29 SPERMATOCELES AND 22 EPIDIDYMAL CYSTS. Mean operative time 39.27 minutes, mean postoperative stay 2.02 days, complication rate 7.3 PERCENT and no cyst recurrence during follow-up; scrotal pain disappeared in 80.4 PERCENT of patients and at a significantly higher rate in those with palpated pain. THERE WAS AN INSIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCE in sperm count, motility, morphology or NEUTRAL ALPHA-GLUCOSIDASE between pre-operation and post-operation at 1-year follow-up; sperm count and neutral alpha-glucosidase in patients with lesions GREATER THAN 2.5 CM were significantly INCREASED after surgery. sourceReferences.citation: Shan CJ, Lucon AM, Pagani R, et al. Sclerotherapy of hydroceles and spermatoceles with alcohol: results and effects on the semen analysis. Int Braz J Urol. 2011 May-Jun;37(3):307-12; discussion 312-33. PMID 21756377.
sourceReferences.note: Uncontrolled treatment series of 69 patients with 114 alcohol sclerotherapy procedures over 84 units between April 2003 and June 2007 for HYDROCele AND/OR SPERMATOCELE, with an overall success rate of 97.62 PERCENT, mean pre-sclerotherapy drained volume 279.82 mL and median follow-up 43 months. Pain was reported immediately after the procedure by 10.14 PERCENT as minor, 4.35 percent as moderate and 2.89 percent as intense. POST-SCLEROTHERAPY SPERMOGRAMS REVEALED REDUCTION of concentration, motility and morphology UP TO 6 MONTHS after the procedure, WITH RETURN TO NORMAL PARAMETERS at the 12th month. Registered because it supplies the TIME COURSE that makes this edge a graded null rather than a flat one. DISCLOSED: an uncontrolled series, hydrocele and spermatocele patients are combined, and the located evidence does not establish that the reduction is fully reversible in every patient.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: Int Braz J Urol. 2011;37(3):307-312. Sclerotherapy of hydroceles and spermatoceles with 99.5 percent alcohol in 69 patients, 114 procedures, 97.62 percent success; post-sclerotherapy spermograms showed reduced concentration, motility and morphology for up to 6 months with return to normal by 12 months.

governanceNotes: IDENTITY SCREEN, batch 86: the catalog is FINER-GRAINED than the located literature for this pair. A spermatocele is an epididymal cyst containing sperm, and the located cohort of 861 men studied them as a single category, EPIDIDYMAL CYST LESIONS INCLUDE BOTH SPERMATOCELES AND EPIDIDYMAL CYSTS, while the catalog carries them as two identities. Because the relationship is containment rather than a secondary condition, NO EDGE HAS BEEN REGISTERED between them and the refusal is declared in the file's todo list so it is durable.

CONTRAST WITH THE IDENTITY-DUPLICATION FINDINGS IN EARLIER BATCHES: this is the mirror case. Earlier batches closed an identity because the catalog was COARSER than the evidence and two names denoted one clinical entity. Here the catalog is FINER than the evidence, which groups the two entities together, and the correct disposition is again to refuse an edge rather than to force one, for the opposite reason.

INCOMING-EDGE MAP, batch 86: this identity had ZERO registered incoming edges and ZERO registered outgoing edges before this batch, so both edges are new. The target varicocele-hydrocele also had ZERO registered incoming edges, so that edge populifies an entirely uncovered identity, while hypogonadism carried three.

TWO GERMAN-LANGUAGE ANCHORS DISCLOSED: the prospective surgical comparison and the management review are both available only in German in the source database, which is recorded so that a qualified-human verifier knows the bibliographic verification was done against the English-language abstract and the German summary rather than a full translation.

EVIDENCE POLARITY DECLARED: one of the two edges is a NULL whose anchor is titled as a null and whose conclusion counsels conservative observation, and the other reports a TRANSIENT post-procedure effect that reverses by 12 months. Neither edge supports a claim that a spermatocele causes disease, and the two negative qualifications, age confounding and a 4 mm median lesion size, are stated on the face of the null edge.
